newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei claws above 20,000 to end firmer.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei claws above 20,000 to end firmer.

text.p: Tokyo stocks closed slightly higher on Wednesday after bouncing back from a morning slump.
Persisting worries over a brokerage scandal pressed the key stock index below the 20,000 barrier for a time, but the decline provided investors with good chances for bargain hunting, brokers said.

The 225-share Nikkei average gained 20.90 points or 0.10 percent to close at 20,196.42, after breaking the 20,000 barrier for the first time since May 28. The index briefly slipped to as low as 19,975.50.
Its September futures ended 120 points higher at 20,220.

"After the Nikkei 225 broke through 20,000, domestic pension funds who are ready to allocate money to stocks, as well as foreign investors, bought shares on dips, as what is most important is the Tokyo stock market's relative cheapness," said Mikio Takada, general manager at Nikko Securities Co Ltd.
